sources_considered.why: Official developer announcement of an implemented same-model price cut.
Dated official baseline for Opus-family input and output prices.
Dated official announcement of lower prices for the successor Opus model.
Its earlier Opus prices are consistent with the baseline, but the Claude 4 announcement provides a closer dated comparison.

receipt.public_excerpt: We’re cutting the price of o3 by 80% and introducing o3-pro in the API, which uses even more compute.

evidence_items.explanation: The announcement says the reduction is in effect and applies to the same o3 model. This establishes OpenAI's part of the prediction.

receipt.public_excerpt: Pricing remains consistent with previous Opus and Sonnet models: Opus 4 at $15/$75 per million tokens (input/output) and Sonnet 4 at $3/$15.

evidence_items.explanation: This establishes the Opus-family baseline of $15 per million input tokens and $75 per million output tokens. Prices had not fallen at this launch.

evidence_items.locator: Opening API availability and pricing paragraph

receipt.public_excerpt: Pricing is now $5/$25 per million tokens—making Opus-level capabilities accessible to even more users, teams, and enterprises.

evidence_items.explanation: Opus 4.5 launched with lower input and output prices than the Opus baseline in e2. This completes the joint forecast under the stated reading that includes successors within a model family.

unresolved_gaps: The price announcements do not establish that DeepSeek caused or compelled either reduction.
The Anthropic evidence concerns a successor model, not repricing identical model weights.
